home.widgetsValuesBody: When this is off, widgets show no numbers and the copy kept for them is deleted.
home.widgetsPrivacy: A widget cannot open the encrypted database. While at least one OpenHoop widget is on your home screen, the app keeps a small unencrypted copy of only these numbers, the day and the sync time (no name, no raw data), and Android keeps the drawn widget images. Removing the last widget or turning values off deletes them.

sleepx.lastNightHint: Heart rate and your night in detail
sleepx.plannerNone: Needs your sleep need and a few recorded nights.
sleepx.noNight: No night was recorded for this day.
sleepx.noHr: No heart rate readings for this night.
stage.title: Sleep stages
stage.edited: Follows your corrected times and uses only what the band measured.
stage.notComputed: Stages appear once this night has been recomputed.
stage.note: An estimate from heart rate and motion, not a sleep lab result. Checked against sleep lab recordings of {subjects} people, it gave the lab's stage for {accuracy}% of 30-second epochs (kappa {kappa}). Deep sleep tends to read high and time awake low. Naps and sleep you add by hand get no stages.
sleepx.typicalNeedHint: Average over the {count} nights before today
sleepx.needNote: Sleep need is a fitted model. OpenHoop shows the total and its history; it does not split it into parts it cannot measure.
sleepx.plannerBasis: Based on {target} of sleep, the median wake time of your last {nights} nights, and the {awake} you usually spend awake in bed.
sleepx.plannerNoNeed: Your sleep need is not known yet, so there is nothing to plan from.
sleepx.plannerNoWake: There are no recorded nights yet to learn your usual wake time from.
sleepx.plannerNote: The bedtime is simple arithmetic on your own recent nights. It does not know your plans for tomorrow.
sleepx.alarmIntro: A silent alarm that buzzes on your wrist. The band runs it by itself, so it also rings when the phone is off or out of range. Smart wake can ring it earlier.
sleepx.alarmExact: Exact time: buzz at the time you choose.
sleepx.alarmGoal: Hit sleep goal: buzz once you have slept your need.
sleepx.alarmWindow: Smart window: buzz at a light moment shortly before the time.
alarm.mode.title: Wake up
alarm.window.title: Window before the alarm
alarm.smart.howWindow: From {start} the phone connects to the band every 5 minutes and rings it at a light moment, or right away when you are already awake. If it cannot tell, the band rings at {time} by itself.
alarm.smart.howGoal: From {start} the phone connects to the band every 5 minutes and rings it once you have slept your sleep need, or right away when you are already awake. Otherwise the band rings at {time} by itself.
alarm.smart.needs: Smart wake needs the phone near the band with Bluetooth on through the night. While it checks, OpenHoop shows a small notification. Light sleep is an estimate (level C).
alarm.smart.unavailable: Smart wake needs Android and permission for exact alarms. On this phone only the exact time works.
alarm.smart.notifyBody: Checking your sleep for the alarm
alarm.status.title: On the band
alarm.status.pending: Not on the band yet. OpenHoop sets it the next time it reaches the band.
alarm.lastStopped: Last rang {when}, stopped early with a double tap
alarm.lastExpired: Last rang {when}, until it stopped by itself
alarm.howBody: The band holds one alarm and rings it by itself at the set time, also when the phone is off or far away. Double-tap the band to stop the buzz. After it has rung, OpenHoop sets the next day's alarm each time it syncs.
alarm.problem.clock: The band's clock is not known yet. Sync once, then set the alarm.
alarm.problem.tooSoon: That is less than a minute away. Choose a later time.
alarm.problem.notArmed: The band did not confirm the alarm. Try again near the band.
alarm.problem.notRung: The band did not play the alarm, so the set time stays on the band.
sleepx.editIntro: Correct the times of a night or add a nap the band missed.
sleepx.editRecalc: Your times replace the detected ones. Sleep need, debt, Sleep score and Readiness are recomputed from that day on. The band readings stay stored, so you can restore the detected times at any time.
sleepx.editPhysio: HRV, resting heart rate and the other night values still come only from what the band measured while you slept.
sleepx.editNone: No sleep was recorded for this day. You can still add a nap.
sleepx.problem.invalid-time: Enter both times as hours and minutes, for example 07:30.
sleepx.problem.end-before-start: The end must be after the start.
sleepx.problem.too-long-nap: A nap can last at most {hours} hours.
sleepx.problem.too-long-night: A sleep can last at most {hours} hours.
sleepx.problem.future: A sleep cannot end in the future.
sleepx.problem.error: Saving did not work. Try again.
readinessx.bandNote: The shaded band on the HRV chart is your normal range: your 30-day average plus and minus one standard deviation.
readinessx.impactsIntro: Compares your next-day readiness after higher and lower days, using only your own recorded data.
readinessx.impactsEmptyBody: A comparison needs at least four days on each side of your own median. You have {days} days so far.
readinessx.impact.loadBody: After days with load above {threshold} (your median), next-day readiness averaged {high}%. After lower days it averaged {low}%.
readinessx.impact.sleepBody: After nights with more than {threshold} h asleep (your median), next-day readiness averaged {high}%. After shorter nights it averaged {low}%.
readinessx.impact.sample: Based on {high} higher days and {low} lower days.
readinessx.impactsNote: These are averages over your own days. Other things changed on the same days, so they do not show cause and effect.
metricDetail.title: Metric
metricDetail.baselineNone: Your normal range needs a few more nights before it can be shown.
metricDetail.bandNote: The shaded band is your normal range, measured at the latest night.
metricDetail.meaning.hrv: The time between two heartbeats is never exactly the same. HRV measures how much it varies. A rested body varies more, so a number above your own usual is a good sign.
metricDetail.meaning.rhr: Your heart rate once your body has settled during sleep. Below your own usual often means you are well rested. A rise of a few beats over several days can come with stress, short sleep or a cold.
metricDetail.meaning.resp: How many breaths you take per minute while asleep. It stays very steady for most people, so a clear jump from your usual is worth noticing. It can change when you are unwell.
metricDetail.meaning.spo2: How much of your blood is carrying oxygen while you sleep. It normally stays high and steady. This is a wellness reading from a wrist sensor, not a medical measurement.
metricDetail.meaning.temp: Skin temperature on its own says little; the change from your own baseline is what matters. A raised value can come with illness, alcohol or a warm room.
metricDetail.method.hrv: OpenHoop works this out from the band's beat-to-beat timing while you sleep. A wellness number, not a medical one.
metricDetail.method.rhr: OpenHoop takes the lowest steady stretch of your heart rate while you sleep.
metricDetail.method.resp: OpenHoop reads it from the small rhythm your breathing leaves in your heartbeat.
metricDetail.method.spo2: Reported by the band itself. OpenHoop shows it as received.
metricDetail.method.temp: The band measures skin temperature. OpenHoop compares it with your own nights.

jetlag.intro: Plan small daily shifts of your sleep and light before, during and after a trip across time zones.
jetlag.disclaimer: This is general guidance based on published research on the body clock. It is not medical advice and does not cover melatonin, caffeine or any medication. Talk to a doctor if you have a sleep or health condition, and do not drive when you are drowsy.
jetlag.source: Based on Eastman and Burgess, "How to travel the world without jet lag", Sleep Medicine Clinics 2009;4(2):241-255: move sleep about 1 hour per day eastward and 1 to 2 hours per day westward, and use bright and dim light to help the shift. OpenHoop uses 1 and 1.5 hours.
jetlag.departureHint: Date as YYYY-MM-DD and time as HH:MM, both in your home time zone.
jetlag.preDaysFewer: Fewer days to adjust before leaving
jetlag.preDaysMore: More days to adjust before leaving
jetlag.anchorHistory: Filled in from your last {nights} nights: the wake time is your typical one, the bedtime is that minus your sleep need and the time you usually lie awake in bed. You can change both.
jetlag.anchorEntered: The plan uses the times you entered.
jetlag.anchorNoHistory: There is not enough sleep history yet, so the plan uses the times you enter. Enter the times you usually sleep.
jetlag.problem.invalid-date: Enter the departure date as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 2026-03-10.
jetlag.problem.invalid-time: Enter the departure time as hours and minutes, for example 10:00.
jetlag.problem.invalid-bed: Enter your usual bedtime as hours and minutes, for example 23:00.
jetlag.problem.invalid-wake: Enter your usual wake time as hours and minutes, for example 07:00.
jetlag.problem.same-bed-wake: Bedtime and wake time must be different.
jetlag.planFailed: The plan could not be made from these values.
jetlag.summaryEast: The destination is {shift} ahead of home. Move your sleep earlier by about {rate} per day.
jetlag.summaryWest: The destination is {shift} behind home. Move your sleep later by about {rate} per day.
jetlag.noShift: Both places show the same time on your departure date, so no shift is needed.
jetlag.lightHint: Bright light means daylight outdoors or a very bright room. To avoid it, stay in dim light and wear sunglasses outside.
jetlag.travelNote: On the travel day these times may fall during the flight. Sleep on board around them if you can.
jetlag.adaptedNote: Sleep at your usual times in the local time of your destination.
jetlag.clockChangeHome: Clocks change at home on this day.
jetlag.clockChangeDest: Clocks change at your destination on this day.
jetlag.savedNote: The active plan is stored on this phone only and is part of your export.
